- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.6), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5+ price jumps) by forecasting further increases; cap or dampen subsequent peaks.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.4 or -0.4 to 0.0), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply mild downward bias toward mid-range historical levels.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; add 1–2 day lag correction for short-term spikes.
- When sentiment shifts sharply (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.6), model often misreads direction; align forecast with sentiment reversal within 3–5 days.
- Avoid forecasting extreme outliers (e.g., >+10% or <-10% from recent mean) unless sentiment confirms strong directional bias.
